universal_lens: Laboratory-to-field translation of helmet impact attenuation via angular acceleration reduction and brain injury metric modulation. The universal lens unifies biomechanical impact kinematics and long-term neurodegenerative trajectories via a cumulative damage operator. It maps the high-frequency stochastic impulse of on-field collisions to low-frequency epigenetic decay, establishing an isomorphism between instantaneous rotational acceleration and asymptotic cognitive failure states.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of helmet efficacy using pre/post impact kinematic data and DAMAGE/HARM risk metrics for probabilistic injury prediction. GSI employs conformal Bayesian inference to map laboratory pneumatic ram tests to on-field youth football impacts. By treating helmet attenuation as a latent variable, we construct predictive intervals for head injury criteria, ensuring robust uncertainty quantification across varying impact orientations and speeds.
gse_mapping: Situationally adaptive helmet state transitions based on real-time impact kinematics and athlete-specific biomechanical profiles. GSE models situational state-transitions where protective equipment alters player risk exposure. The engine calculates dynamic hazard potentials by integrating real-time kinematic telemetry with historical neuropsychiatric baselines, optimizing defensive alignments to minimize cumulative rotational acceleration while maintaining competitive tactical integrity.

primitives.name: Laboratory-to-Field Transduction
primitives.verbatim_quote: In a preliminary on-field investigation, we used instrumented mouthguards to monitor head impact magnitude in collegiate linebackers during practice sessions while not wearing the padded helmet shell covers (i.e., bare helmets) for one season and whilst wearing the padded helmet shell covers for another season.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When impact velocity exceeds 7.4 m/s or angular acceleration surpasses 1000 rad/s².

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic mapping between lab-tested angular acceleration reduction and field-based HARM decrease.

primitives.name: Angular Acceleration Attenuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The addition of the padded helmet shell cover was effective in attenuating the magnitude of angular head accelerations and two brain injury risk metrics (DAMAGE, HARM) across most laboratory impact conditions, but did not significantly attenuate linear head accelerations for all helmets.

primitives.assumptions: Linear motion does not influence angular acceleration; helmet cover uniformly affects rotational inertia.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At impact velocities > 5.5 m/s where angular acceleration exceeds 1500 rad/s².

layer2.mapping: Kernel derived from angular acceleration difference to compute injury risk reduction.

primitives.name: HARM Reduction Metric

primitives.breakdown_regime: When v < 3.5 m/s or v > 7.4 m/s due to non-linear behavior beyond tested range.

primitives.name: ImpactConditionEffectOnHarmSignificance
